summary: Redwood SEs walked NexaHealth through OpenTelemetry integration for token-level metrics, tracing, and dashboards in a VPC/on-prem context. Main topics: OTel collector setup, token-level counters, KV cache and batching visibility, quantization signal metrics, and security considerations for private deployments. Agreed next steps: share configs, dashboards, and schedule a pilot benchmark in their VPC.
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-12 15:00 UTC | Duration 54m | Attendees: Sofia Martinez, Daniel Park, Rina Gupta (Redwood) — Priya Kapoor, Liam O'Connor, Marta Ruiz, Samir Patel (NexaHealth)

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining? um we'll go 54 minutes ish, we can run over if needed. quick intros?
[00:10] Priya: hey Priya here, head of platform at NexaHealth, Liam (SRE) and Marta (ML) also on.
[00:15] Liam: hi all.
[00:20] Daniel: dan park, i'm the se on this account, rina here for observability stuff.
[00:28] Priya: goal for today is really to understand how we can get token-level metrics and traces from Redwood runtime into our OTel stack inside our VPC, and what visibility we get into kv-cache and batching.
[00:36] Rina: perfect, we'll cover collector config, metric names, traces span schema, dashboards, and security controls for VPC/on-prem.
[00:45] Sofia: quick background: NexaHealth wants to run sensitive inference in a private deployment and needs per-token latency and failure visibility to tie to SLOs.

[02:05] Daniel: ok jumping in, at a high level Redwood emits three things: structured traces for request lifecycle, token-level counters/histograms, and runtime metrics (gpu utilization, queue length, kv cache hit/miss). we can push via OTLP to your collector inside the VPC.
[02:40] Marta: are the token metrics per model version or per endpoint? we have multi-model routing so need per-model breakdown.
[02:50] Rina: yes per model-version and per-route and we include tags for model_id, variant, sequence_length bucket, and deployment node id. sometimes the tag names in the exporter get munged, we've seen auto-transcribe issues so double-check.
[03:30] Liam: how about overhead — do token-level traces add a lot of latency? we can't increase tail latency.
[03:40] Daniel: great question. token-level counters are exported asynchronously, they're counters/histograms aggregated on the host and flushed in batch to OTLP. tracing spans are lightweight — we sample depending on config. default is 1% full trace sampling plus 100% short span emission for error paths. typical additional p99 overhead is single-digit ms if collector is local — network hops increase it.
[04:20] Priya: local collector inside our VPC then. what about TLS and mTLS to the collector?
[04:30] Rina: we support OTLP over HTTP and gRPC with TLS. for Private we can do mTLS to your collector; for on-prem package we can hook into your internal CA and KMS for keys. we'll share a sample config.

[06:00] Daniel: now KV cache observability — we emit per-request kv cache hits, prefix cache hits, and eviction counters. typical panels: kv_hit_rate by model/route, avg_kv_latency, hot-key skew. we also surface cache warm-up traces.
[06:40] Marta: can we correlate kv cache misses to increased token latency in the same trace?
[06:50] Rina: yes, span attributes include kv_cache.status=miss/hit and kv_latency_ms, also we add a boolean span event when we go to storage fallback. correlation works in traces if you keep the same trace id across retries.
[07:20] Liam: do you emit batching metrics? we need to see batch size distribution and queue wait time to tune autoscaler.
[07:30] Daniel: we expose batch_size_histogram, queue_wait_ms, batch_formation_time, and per-node inflight_requests. Grafana dashboards can show heatmaps of batch size vs latency.
[08:05] Priya: sounds good. what about quantization telemetry — we want to monitor quality regressions after quantizing a model.
[08:15] Rina: we expose quality proxy metrics when you enable eval hooks: token_confidence_score distributions, ngram divergence from baseline, and can attach eval ids to traces. for actual model evals we recommend running periodic eval jobs and pushing results as custom metrics.
[08:50] Marta: token_confidence_score — is that inferred or from model logits? we need something consistent.
[08:55] Daniel: it's based on normalized logit deltas we compute in runtime — rough proxy not a perfect QA, but useful for regressions. we'll document the formula and you can switch it off if it's noisy.

[10:10] Priya: security: we need audit logs and proof of non-persistent data retention. how do traces and metrics interact with data residency?
[10:25] Rina: metrics are non-PHI by default; we strip PII from traces unless you enable full-logging for debugging. In Private/VPC we keep telemetry inside your network; for Hosted we'd route to Redwood telemetry which you said you don't want. We'll also sign off on retention windows and provide audit logs for export.
[11:00] Samir: for on-prem we'd like to use our HSM (YubiHSM) for keys and a SAML SSO for console admin. support?
[11:10] Daniel: yes KMS/HSM integrations supported, SAML for console and RBAC — we'll share the enterprise security pack.

[12:40] Sofia: i want to demo the dashboard quickly — dan you have the sample grafana?
[12:50] Daniel: pulling it up — sharing link in chat (sent). panel 1: token-rate by model; panel 2: token-p99 latency; panel 3: kv hit/miss; panel 4: batch size heatmap; panel 5: quantization delta metrics.
[13:30] Priya: (looking) ok i like the kv heatmap — can we slice by cohort/user-defined tag?
[13:40] Rina: yes you can pass custom request attributes that become labels: customer_id, project, request_tier — small note, high cardinality tags can increase cardinality costs, we recommend a few cardinal dimensions.

[15:05] Marta: on sampling — you said 1% full traces by default; can we do rules like sample all errors and 100% of requests for a test route?
[15:15] Daniel: absolutely, sampling rules are configurable per-route. you can do rate-based and rule-based (match route, model, status). for pilot we often recommend high-sample on test routes, plus error-only on prod.

[17:00] Liam: about telemetry volume — if we push OTLP directly from 20 nodes with token metrics at high qps, how do you avoid blowing our collector?
[17:10] Rina: we provide batching in the exporter, aggregation on-host, and we support remote_write or ingest-side rate-limits. best practice: run a local otel-collector with resource limits, ingest aggregated metrics and use delta counters. we'll share a sample collector config with throttling and receiver limits.
[18:00] Priya: can you show example metric names? we need to map them into our schema.
[18:10] Daniel: sure — examples: redwood.runtime.token_count, redwood.runtime.token_latency_ms_bucket, redwood.runtime.kv_cache_hit_total, redwood.runtime.batch_size_histogram, redwood.runtime.model_quantization_delta. tags: model_id, model_version, route, node_id, seq_len_bucket. note: some older exports used redwood.inference.* — we'll include both for compatibility.
[19:05] Marta: great. can we add a generated metric that approximates per-request token cost? we'd like to backcharge teams.
[19:15] Rina: yes we can expose token_cost_estimate per-request using your pricing model or our default. it won't be billing-legal but good for internal chargebacks.

[21:00] Daniel: deployment specifics for VPC/private: in VPC we run the control plane managed but telemetry endpoint is your collector endpoint. for full on-prem we ship the runtime and collector as part of the package. the main differences are networking (eg no egress) and how keys are stored.
[21:40] Priya: for the pilot we want to run in our AWS VPC and use our otel-collector + grafana in EKS — ok?
[21:50] Sofia: yes that's our typical setup — we tested with EKS collectors. we'll provide helm chart snippets.

[24:00] Liam: what about offline replay — we want to replay traffic and reconstruct traces/metrics to debug regressions.
[24:10] Daniel: you can export the trace ids and event logs; we also provide a lightweight replay harness that replays requests against a pinned model version and emits synthetic traces/metrics. it's part of our optimize toolkit.

[26:20] Marta: curious — when KV cache misses cause extra storage fetches, do you surface backend storage latency as part of the trace?
[26:30] Rina: yes we instrument the storage call as a child span with backend.host and backend.latency_ms and include error codes. helps identify slow tuners.

[28:00] Priya: can we redact certain attributes from spans before they hit our collector? e.g., user IDs?
[28:10] Daniel: yes you can configure attribute processors in the otel-collector to mask or drop attributes. runtime can also avoid emitting them. we'll document recommended processors.

[30:00] Sofia: ok let's talk alarms and SLOs — customers often want per-route p99 < 200ms and token-error-rate < 0.1%. how do we surface that?
[30:15] Rina: build alerting rules against token_latency p99 and token_error_rate metrics; we export error counters with labels error_type and stage (parsing, kv, decode). Grafana + alertmanager or your cloud native alerts can fire.

[32:00] Liam: any gotchas with quantized models and metric interpretation?
[32:10] Daniel: quantization sometimes changes token timing (lots of small speedups but occasional decode stalls) and modifies confidence scores; watch token_confidence_score drift and avg_decode_time_ms. also watch for increased max_memory metrics on some kernels.

[34:30] Priya: how fast can we iterate? say we want to run a pilot for 2 weeks, run experiments, then decide on Dedicated.
[34:40] Sofia: typical pilot 2–4 weeks. we can support a short Dedicated trial, provide runbooks, and an SE to help tune batching/kv profiles.

[36:10] Marta: can we instrument prompts or prompt-sets as tags to compare quality across versions?
[36:20] Rina: yes low-cardinality prompt-set tags are supported; we include eval hooks to bucket results per-prompt-set.

[38:00] Samir: compliance — will telemetry contain PHI? need to be sure for HIPAA.
[38:10] Daniel: by default telemetry strips PII; for PHI you must configure the runtime to remove or hash patient identifiers. in private/on-prem we can attest to telemetry staying inside your VPC and provide SOC2 artifacts.

[40:00] Priya: ok one more practical: how do we onboard the otel collector? example helm and resource sizes?
[40:10] Rina: we'll share the helm chart; recommended for our qps: 3 replica collector deployment in EKS for medium load, 8 cpu/16gb memory per replica as a starting point — but depends on cardinality and metric volume. config will include receivers: otlp, processors: batch, memory_limiter, exporters: prometheus_remote_write (optional).

[43:00] Daniel: quick demo of a trace — showing a request with kv miss, batch delay, and quantization delta attached. (screen) you can see span timeline, attributes, and the token_latency waterfall.
[44:10] Marta: ok that waterfall is helpful. can we export raw spans to Jaeger as well?
[44:20] Rina: yes OTLP -> Jaeger option supported.

[46:00] Priya: any performance impact running with full telemetry vs minimal? numbers?
[46:10] Daniel: full verbose tracing does add CPU and memory; our internal benchmarks show 3–7% CPU increase with 100% trace sampling and ~5–10% network egress increase. for most production use we recommend sampled traces plus full metrics.

[48:00] Sofia: recap?
[48:10] Priya: we need sample configs, dashboards, security docs, and to schedule pilot in VPC.
[48:20] Sofia: action items — we'll send collector config, grafana dashboards, and pilot runbook. dan will share the sample metrics list.

[50:00] Daniel: i'll put everything in a confluence link and share via email — also including helm chart.
[50:10] Marta: thanks, please include example queries for the dashboards.
[50:20] Rina: will do.

[52:00] Priya: ok last thing — cost: how to estimate telemetry cost for us?
[52:10] Sofia: we'll include recommended retention and cardinality knobs and a cost estimate based on the metrics volume we discussed. not billing, but an operational cost estimate.
[53:00] Sofia: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and the pilot scheduling.
[53:10] Priya: thanks all.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (e.g., "K V cache" spelled, minor name mis-hears). Shared artifacts: link to demo grafana (sent in chat), sample helm chart (to be shared).
